title: Trace-one Noetherian invariant finiteness
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let a finite group $G$ act on $R$ by ring automorphisms, and put $A=R^G=\{r\in R:g(r)=r\text{ for all }g\in G\}$. Suppose there exists $a\in R$ with $\sum_{g\in G}g(a)=1$. Then $A$ is Noetherian and $R$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The action need not be faithful, and neither invertibility of $|G|$ in $R$ nor an algebra of finite type over a base ring is assumed.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(b), printed p.75, finite tame strict-local invariant quotient: agent-supplied algebraic finiteness input, in the more general trace-one form. The skew-group idempotent proof is written in report.md; this formulation is not claimed to be a theorem explicitly stated in ILO.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8. Supporting input: Exposé VI §3.2, printed p.74 (admissible underlying scheme quotient), and proof 3.7(b), printed p.75 (finite tame strict-local invariant quotient). Scheme-theoretic quotient ingredient, with tameness retained for Noetherian finiteness. Algebraic input isolated for the tame admissible underlying scheme quotient: Trace-one Noetherian invariant finiteness.
